claims.text: Incorporating machine-learning models can significantly improve the accuracy of melting-temperature and other melting-property predictions for high-entropy alloys.
Incorporating machine-learning models can significantly improve the computational efficiency of melting-property predictions for high-entropy alloys.
The proposed models use Hölder means of elemental properties and structural properties as inputs.
Relevant elemental descriptors include group number, atomic radius, and electronegativity.
Relevant structural descriptors include cohesive energy and density.
Machine-learning models can predict shear and bulk moduli of disordered high-entropy alloys with good accuracy.
The demonstrated ability to predict elastic moduli can be extended to predicting melting temperatures and other melting properties.
The proposed method will be more accurate than current conventional melting-property prediction methods.
The proposed method will be more computationally efficient than current conventional melting-property prediction methods.
The hypothesis is intended to apply at room temperature and across various compositional ranges.
Validity is limited to high-entropy alloys within specific compositional ranges and structural-property domains.
Prediction accuracy may depend on the quality and quantity of the training data.
The models may not generalize reliably to different high-entropy-alloy systems.
A falsification benchmark should compare machine-learning and conventional melting-temperature predictions over high-entropy alloys with varying compositions.
Prediction accuracy should be evaluated using mean absolute error and root mean square error.
Failure to obtain significant improvements in both accuracy and computational efficiency relative to conventional methods would falsify the hypothesis.
